title: AI developer boom could create 40 million digital jobs across Africa – World Bank
key_facts: The World Bank's October 2026 Africa Economic Update, "Building AI Readiness", says Africa's AI economy could create 35 to 40 million digital jobs.
It could also generate nearly $150 billion in annual tax revenue.
The gain depends on closing gaps in infrastructure, computing capacity, data and digital skills.
At current readiness, AI is estimated to add only 0.2% to 4% to cumulative GDP in Sub-Saharan Africa over the next decade.
About 900 million Africans are offline; Africa has about 18% of the world's people but 0.6% of data-centre capacity.
Only about 2.6% of Sub-Saharan jobs face near-term automation risk, against 14.2% in high-income economies.
quote_evidence: Africa’s emerging artificial intelligence economy could create 35 to 40 million digital jobs and generate nearly $150 billion in annual tax revenue.
At current levels of preparedness, however, AI is estimated to contribute only 0.2 percent to 4 percent of cumulative GDP over the next decade in Sub-Saharan Africa.
why_it_matters_hint: A large job-creation estimate for Africa that depends on electricity, connectivity and skills being built first.
